title: Differential latency fingerprinting and rate-classification probes for VPC workers
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Problem: Existing VPC health probes treat all traffic from a private deployment as a single homogeneous stream. This leads to noisy alerts and either missed early-warning signals for high-rate customers or false positives for low-rate tenants. Goal: build composite probes that (1) fingerprint request latency shapes per route/tenant, (2) classify traffic into dynamic rate buckets, and (3) emit SLO signals and saturation alarms that adapt sensitivity by rate class. The overall aim is earlier detection of degradation for high-throughput classes while reducing alert churn for low-throughput workloads.
acceptance_criteria: Latency fingerprinting agent deployed as sidecar to VPC workers and producing per-route latency histograms to REDIS or telemetry gateway
Rate-classification labels appear in Prometheus metrics and are joinable with existing token-throughput metrics
SLO rules in Grafana/Alertmanager that use rate-classed p50/p90/p99 with separate thresholds for each bucket
Automated Terraform module changes add the sidecar container and RBAC for telemetry ingestion to private clusters
Playbook updated: for each rate class describe runbook steps and rollback thresholds
Canary rollout completed: 10% of private fleet for 48 hours with no customer-impacting alerts
implementation_notes: Fingerprinting: use reservoir-sampled HDR histograms per route keyed by (customer_id, model_route, seq_len_bucket)
Rate buckets: define ephemeral classes (idle, low, medium, high, burst) from 1m token-rate percentiles; recompute every 5m
Probe evaluation: compute differential delta between current fingerprint and baseline using Kolmogorov-Smirnov distance and waterfall of thresholds per bucket
Alert semantics: high bucket p99 crossing threshold -> immediate paging; medium crossing -> slack channel with auto-snooze; low -> ticket only
Storage: retain 1h raw histograms, 7d aggregated fingerprints, and 90d aggregated SLO windows in telemetry store
Terraform: add module flag private_health_fingerprint_enabled and inject sidecar via k8s_deployment_patch; ensure KMS policy allows telemetry sidecar to push encrypted blobs
Performance: sidecar must sample less than 1% CPU overhead at 90th percentile traffic for high bucket — profile during canary
test_plan: Unit tests for fingerprinting and KS-distance computation
Integration test in staging: synthetic traffic generator that produces multiple rate classes and controlled latency regressions
Chaos test: introduce transient GC pauses and verify classification and alert behavior
Load test: validate 95th CPU and memory overheads for sidecar at 3x expected production peak
Terraform plan/apply dry-run validation and drift detection in staging cluster
rollout_plan: Feature flag gated rollout via console (private_health_fingerprint_enabled)
Canary cohort: select 10% of customers across rate classes; monitor for 48h
Step to 50% after 72h if no critical alerts and sidecar resource usage within limits
Full rollout with automated rollback if >2 critical pages in 1h or sustained SLO deterioration for >30m
Post-rollout 30d review to tune KS thresholds and bucket boundaries
